products.summary: The cheapest single-unit 120/240 V split-phase power station with 6,000 W of continuous output on any maker store on 2026-11-06. 3,600 Wh of LiFePO4 on wheels, 9,000 W surge for pump and compressor starts, 2,200 W wall charging and expansion to 57.6 kWh.
products.fit: Outage backup for a 240 V well pump, dryer or mini-split plus a refrigerator and lights, or RV and workshop use, when you want 6,000 W at 240 V without paying $2,700 or more.
caveats: Pre-sale on 2026-11-06: the store listed shipping around November 26.
OSCAL does not name the 240 V receptacle type. Confirm NEMA 14-50 versus L14-30 with support before buying an inlet cord or transfer switch.
A lab test measured about 2,960 Wh usable (82% of rated) on average, and only 66% at a slow 100 W AC load.
No OSCAL app; the unit pairs through the generic Smart Life app with basic controls.
No IP rating; splash and dust resistant only, so keep it sheltered.
OSCAL's own pages disagree on warranty wording (5 years in the spec table, 4-year+ in a comparison table); the policy page says 60 months.
